title: TRACE: Artifact-Robust Statistical Shape Modeling from Imperfect Surface Scans - A Case Study in Craniosynostosis 3D Photography
abstract: arXiv:2608.22131v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Craniosynostosis severity analysis increasingly relies on statistical shape models (SSMs) to quantify cranial morphology, but most existing workflows depend on computed tomography or heavily curated three-dimensional (3D) photographs. Raw clinical 3D photographs provide a radiation-free and repeatable alternative, yet often contain shoulders, hands, hair, clothing, scanner noise, and incomplete boundaries that corrupt correspondences. We introduce the Template-constrained Robust Artifact-aware Correspondence Estimation (TRACE) framework, an unsupervised method for constructing SSMs directly from artifact-contaminated clinical 3D head photographs. TRACE predicts sparse anatomically corresponding head-surface control points from the raw point cloud, refines them through a coarse-to-fine Surface-Aware Deformation cascade, and uses thin-plate spline warping to deform a clean template mesh into a subject-specific head reconstruction. translated_abstract: 摘要：颅缝早闭的严重程度分析越来越依赖于统计形状模型（SSMs）来量化颅骨形态，但大多数现有工作流程依赖于计算机断层扫描或经过严格处理的三维（3D）照片。原始临床3D照片提供了一种无辐射且可重复的替代方案，但通常包含肩膀、手、头发、衣物、扫描仪噪声和不完整边界，这些都会破坏对应关系。我们引入了模板约束的鲁棒伪影感知对应估计（TRACE）框架，这是一种无监督方法，可直接从受伪影污染的临床3D头部照片中构建SSMs。TRACE从原始点云中预测稀疏的解剖学对应头部表面控制点，通过从粗到细的表面感知变形级联进行细化，并使用薄板样条扭曲将干净的模板网格变形为特定受试者的头部重建。这使t
tldr: 本文提出了一种名为TRACE的无监督框架，能够直接从含伪影的临床3D头部照片中构建统计形状模型，通过预测稀疏对应点并利用变形和薄板样条扭曲实现鲁棒的头颅重建，从而克服了传统方法对CT或高度处理数据的依赖。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TRACE, an unsupervised framework that constructs statistical shape models directly from artifact-contaminated clinical 3D head photographs by predicting sparse correspondence points and using deformation with thin-plate spline warping, overcoming reliance on CT or heavily curated data.
